feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: On the campaign trail, Trump delivers his greatest political hits and mourns end of rallies
entry.summary: President Trump is campaigning hard in the midterms. Supporters are showing up, in part because this could be the last chance to see him holding the large rallies that have been his trademark.

entry.title: The numbers say the U.S. economy is strong. These Americans aren't feeling it
entry.summary: The latest data from the Commerce Department reveals a strong economy. But Americans say they're not feeling that.

entry.title: Why voter turnout of Palestinian citizens of Israel surged during its latest election
entry.summary: NPR's Juana Summers talks with Dianna Buttu, Palestinian Canadian human rights attorney, about the vote in Israel, which saw a surge in turnout among Palestinian citizens of Israel.

entry.title: Some rural Republicans in California say redistricting has left them without a voice
entry.summary: California's far northeastern corner used to be a reliably red congressional district. But Proposition 50 carved it up, meaning many voters there may soon have a Democrat representing them in D.C.

entry.title: Lost your spark? The "silent sister" of depression, and a quiz to spot her
entry.summary: Always busy, but rarely joyful? Allison Aubrey and Juana Summers discuss a tool to spot "high functioning depression."

entry.title: Even birds get jet lagged, study shows
entry.summary: A species of seabirds appears to become disoriented on flights back to its nest due to shifting time zones.

entry.title: Fishing is a key issue in Alaska's tight U.S. Senate race
entry.summary: Alaska's U.S. Senate race is embroiled in an emotional fight over fish. Many in the state rely upon salmon to feed their families but those fish and others are increasingly hard to find.

entry.title: A breakthrough for the group on the trail of Chinese hackers
entry.summary: Chinese government hackers are secretly burrowing into critical networks using creative new methods.

entry.title: Despite her own hard times, a Maryland woman became a leading data center activist
entry.summary: Despite her hard financial times, a Maryland woman became a leading local data center activist — an example of the way the issue has prompted people to get involved.

entry.title: Meet the creator of 'Spooky Lake Month,' exploring the world's haunted hydrology
entry.summary: Geo Rutherford is a TikTok creator whose annual series "Spooky Lake Month" has amassed her millions of followers.
